nodes.title: director19: Brain v6.10 + follow-up, Studio P6, Learning D13 on int/r6 d0dd1d5a0, run by main, 16 lessons, 1,544 calls ~$1.071 (a first attempt was killed by a worker restart after 4 lessons, ~$0.25, unused); counted by hand by 4 Claude judges on Opus 5.5 (0-based rows): beats 289/290, verdicts 262/262, misgrades 0, false keys 0, unsaid boards 0, held cost 0; words against board 1 by main's ruling (c4 steady 62, a planned board change not drawn) and 2 by the judges' count (c6 steady 18, the honest 'no second picture' line on the hexagon, ruled an unmet request, not a contradiction); picture requests 15/16 drew a true split view, 0 picture lines with no view (director18: 9); no card answered right was posed again. Axes: listening c4 3 (was 3.5), c5-t01 3, c5-t02 3, c6 3.5; register 3 in all four (c5-t01 and c6 fell from 3.5); promises c4 3.5, others 3. Main's check after judging, same tree: the harness's dry matrix (16 lessons, model stubbed) runs in 27 s and shows the doubled park sentence in 7 lessons, the orphan aside return in 11 and 'Phir se dekho:' 42 times in all 16; the other code-written faults were not checked dry.

Script walk v6.11: the dry matrix as a gate; responses compiled, not chosen; the aside return gets its own turn. G2: the 16 lessons run dry inside test:all with one predicate file that throws on each fault director19 found (a sentence twice in a turn; a joint form reused before the others; an unfilled slot or the child's first-person words in her mouth; a re-pose frame on a first posing; a question to the child plus a card in one turn; key + new point + new card in one turn; a give-up with spent help answered without the key; clarify at a check-in answered with a card; a planned board change not drawn; a board change under a joint; a worked example closed without its answer; an English word beside its Hindi twin); no paid run while it is red; every later fix adds its predicate first. C1: a pure compileScript turns each unit into an explicit map, part x request x help state -> exactly one response built from authored fields; the validator fails a hole or a double; the walk looks up, it does not decide; a dry-matrix predicate checks each turn against the compiled response. J2: the return says one authored question on {aside} and stops, no card that turn; her answer to the child's reply is one reply-model sentence behind a predicate (<= 14 words, no question, no taste claim, uses a content word of the reply), else a neutral joint; {said} leaves the authored forms (Learning D14); joint forms rotate. F1: Brain lists every code-written sentence in say.js with counts; each is authored per topic with three forms, kept as a neutral frame of <= 3 words, or removed; the AI-identity line is not touched (safety floor frozen). Clauses of v6.10: 1 not triggered (0 picture lines with no view); 2 triggered (listening < 3.5 in three topics) taken as C1; 3 triggered (register < 3.5 in all four) taken as F1; 4 not triggered. Order: G2 and the rendering fixes first, released as release 17 when the dry matrix is green; C1, J2, F1 follow and director20 judges them. The regenerated 30-topic batch stays held from children. Why: four runs of hand fixes in one 4,000-line state machine each fixed their targets and moved or added faults, and replay tests written with each fix passed while the next paid run failed on the same row (clarify at a check-in: third run). Reverse if in director20: dry matrix green and the paid run shows a fault on its list -> that predicate is wrong, no paid run until it fails on the paid row; listening < 3.5 with compiled responses -> the failing cells are re-authored by Learning, runtime untouched; the model-written aside reply fails its predicate more than 1 in 5 or is wrong about the child's words -> back to a neutral joint and aside listening becomes its own work; any misgrade, unsaid board or held cost -> as before.

Proving a walk fix with a test that replays a recorded lesson up to one row and checks the next move (the form of the tests behind v6.6 to v6.10). What broke: the clarify-at-a-check-in row was reported fixed in v6.10 with a test on director18's rows c4 steering 6 and c5-t01 steering 6, and failed on those same two rows in director19, its third failing run; the paid run walks a new lesson whose earlier turns differ from the recording. And no test of that form can see faults nobody listed: a park sentence said twice in a row, a re-pose frame on a first posing, a return stacked on a card (all new in director19, all visible in a free 27-second dry run of the 16 lessons). Replays stay as regression pins; they are not evidence that the next run will pass. Evidence for a walk fix is a predicate over the whole dry matrix, seen failing before the fix.

## `dc-r7-script-walk-v6-11` (2026-11-10)

The dry matrix as a gate; responses compiled, not chosen; the aside return gets its own turn.

- **G2:** the 16 lessons run dry inside `test:all`, with one predicate file that throws on each fault director19 found. No paid run while it is red. Every later fix adds its predicate first and sees it fail.
- **C1:** a pure `compileScript` turns each unit into an explicit map: part × request × help state → exactly one response, built from authored fields. The validator fails a hole or a double. The walk looks the response up; it does not decide.
- **J2:** the return says one authored question on `{aside}` and stops. Her answer to the child's reply is one reply-model sentence behind a predicate, else a neutral joint. `{said}` leaves the authored forms.
- **F1:** every code-written sentence is listed with its count, then authored per topic, kept as a neutral frame of three words or fewer, or removed. The AI-identity line is not touched.

**Why:** four runs of hand fixes in one 4,000-line state machine each fixed their targets and moved or added faults elsewhere, and the replay tests written with each fix passed while the next paid run failed.

**Clauses of v6.10:** 1 not triggered; 2 (listening) taken as C1; 3 (register) taken as F1; 4 not triggered.

**Order:** G2 and the rendering fixes first, released as release 17 when the dry matrix is green. C1, J2 and F1 follow; director20 judges them. The regenerated 30-topic batch stays held from children.

**Reverse if, in director20:**
- the dry matrix was green and the paid run shows a fault on its list: that predicate is wrong, and no paid run until it fails on the paid row;
- listening is below 3.5 with compiled responses: the failing cells are re-authored by Learning, and the runtime is not touched;
- the model-written aside reply fails its predicate more than one time in five, or is wrong about the child's words: back to a neutral joint, and listening to an aside becomes its own piece of work;
- any misgrade, unsaid board or held cost: as before.

## `rj-r7-replay-tests-as-proof-of-walk-fixes` (2026-11-10)

The tried approach: proving a walk fix with a test that replays a recorded lesson up to one row and checks the next move (the tests behind v6.6 to v6.10).

**What broke:**
- The clarify-at-a-check-in row was reported fixed in v6.10, with a test on director18's rows c4 steering 6 and c5-t01 steering 6. It failed on those same two rows in director19, its third failing run. The paid run walks a new lesson whose earlier turns differ from the recording.
- No test of that form can see a fault nobody listed: a park sentence said twice in a row, a re-pose frame on a first posing, a return stacked on a card. All three were new in director19 and all three are visible in a free 27-second dry run.

Replays stay as regression pins. Evidence for a walk fix is a predicate over the whole dry matrix, seen failing before the fix.
